C67.content_en:
Ways to track how mentions change over time — and how the main tools compare

When you choose a topic for a book or article, you want to know whether the word is growing or fading online. Enter a keyword and this tool tabulates the mention count and the positive, negative and neutral counts for each of the last 12 months.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.0244 per call (measured), roughly 40 per $1Monthly mention counts and sentiment counts in a table. Save as CSV
Google TrendsFreeCompares relative search interest over time; the peak is scaled to 100 (per Google's page)
Google AlertsFreeEmails you when new pages appear; no monthly tallies. It does not catch every mention (per Ahrefs' guide)
Search monthly and note the count yourself (by hand)FreeBecomes a record if you keep going, but cannot look back

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • The past 12 months in one call. You can look back even if you never kept records.
  • Counts as DataForSEO tallies them. For "Starbucks" the figure moved from about 139 thousand in April 2026 to about 475 thousand in October (measured).
  • Sentiment counts per month. Positive, negative and neutral counts line up month by month.
  • About $0.0244 per call. Roughly 40 per $1, so you can try many words.
  • Save as CSV. Turn it into a chart in a spreadsheet.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want a trend for pages in one language only → this trend is not filtered by language. We tried a language filter in testing and the numbers did not change (measured).
  • You want search volume over time → this counts mentions on pages, not searches. Google Trends fits better.
  • You want daily movement → this tool is monthly.
  • The current month is partial and comes out small, so it is left out of the table. The table shows the last 12 complete months.

This tool does one thing: show a keyword's mention count and sentiment counts for each of the last 12 months.

FAQ

Why monthly?

This tool is set to return 12 months, month by month. There is no daily or weekly switch.

What is the unit of the mention count?

The number of mentions as DataForSEO tallies them. See DataForSEO's documentation for the exact counting rules.

Can I limit it to one language?

We tried a filter and the numbers did not change, so this tool does not filter.

How long does it take?

We measured about 10 seconds for "Starbucks" and about 21 seconds for a Japanese keyword.

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?

C68.content_en:
Ways to list local businesses — and how the main tools compare

A B2B sales rep wants to find visit candidates in bulk. Pick a business-type word and an area, and this tool lists up to 100 local businesses with name, category, address, phone, website and rating.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.048 per 100 rows (measured), roughly 20 calls per $1100 businesses with name, category, address, phone, website and rating in a table. Save as CSV
Google Maps search (by hand)FreeYou copy what you see one by one; turning it into a table is manual
Google Places APIPay per use (see the official site for pricing)A way to pull Google's place data from code; it takes development work
OutscraperSee the official site for pricingA service that collects Google Maps data (see the official site for features)

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • 100 rows in one call. Searching "ラーメン" in Tokyo returned 100 rows in about 3 to 6 seconds (measured).
  • Phone and website included. Of those 100 rows, 87 had a phone number, 90 had a website and 95 had a rating (measured).
  • About $0.048 per call. Roughly 20 per $1, so you can try many areas.
  • Just pick the area from a list. No need to look up latitude and longitude.
  • Save as CSV. A draft for your sales list.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want Japanese spellings → many rows have English names, addresses and categories (e.g. "Koto City", "Ramen restaurant").
  • You want to narrow exactly by business type → the type word is a text search. Of the 100 rows for "ラーメン", 70 had the category ramen restaurant (measured). Parking lots and the like are mixed in.
  • You want a town not on the list → the area is chosen from 12 major cities.
  • You want more than 100 → this tool stops at 100. The matches for "ラーメン" around Tokyo Station were 624 (measured).

This tool does one thing: list up to 100 businesses in a chosen area that match a business-type word.

FAQ

How wide is the area?

A 5 km radius around the centre of the chosen city. For Tokyo, the centre is Tokyo Station.

Why are some rows in English?

In our test all 100 categories were in English, 29 names and 59 addresses were in Japanese. The data is probably stored that way, but we have not confirmed why.

How do I write the business-type word?

An ordinary word such as "ラーメン" or "美容室". Businesses whose description matches the word appear.

What do blank phone or website cells mean?

Nothing was registered. Of the 100 rows, 13 had no phone and 10 had no website (measured).

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?
